Question:
Let \(m \gt 1\) and \(n \gt 1\) be integers. Suppose that the product of the solutions for \(x\) of the equation

\[ \begin{aligned} &8(\log_n x)(\log_m x) - 7\log_n x \\ &\quad {}- 6\log_m x - 2013 = 0 \end{aligned} \]

is the smallest possible integer. What is \(m + n?\)
Solution:
A product of positive solutions becomes a sum after taking logarithms. Set
\[
t=\log_2 x,\qquad A=\log_2 m,\qquad B=\log_2 n.
\]
Here \(x>0\), and \(A,B>0\) because \(m,n>1\). Changing bases and multiplying by \(AB\) transforms the equation into
\[
8t^2-(7A+6B)t-2013AB=0.
\]
Its discriminant is
\[
(7A+6B)^2+4\cdot8\cdot2013AB>0,
\]
so it has two distinct real roots \(t_1,t_2\). Each gives exactly one positive solution \(x_i=2^{t_i}\) of the original equation.

Expanding \(8(t-t_1)(t-t_2)\) shows that the coefficient of \(t\) is \(-8(t_1+t_2)\). Comparing coefficients therefore gives
\[
t_1+t_2=\frac{7A+6B}{8}.
\]
If \(K=x_1x_2\), then
\[
K=2^{t_1+t_2}=m^{7/8}n^{6/8},
\qquad K^8=m^7n^6.
\]
We now use the requirement that \(K\) be an integer.

Choose any prime \(p\) dividing \(m\), and let \(u,v,w\) be its exponents in \(m,n,K\), respectively. Thus \(u\ge1\), \(v\ge0\), and
\[
8w=7u+6v.
\]
The right side is even only if \(u\) is even, so \(u\ge2\). If \(w\le3\), then \(7u\le24\), forcing \(u=2\). But for \(w=1,2,3\), the resulting values
\[
6v=8w-14=-6,\ 2,\ 10
\]
are never nonnegative multiples of 6. Hence \(w\ge4\), and every integer product satisfies
\[
K\ge p^4\ge2^4=16.
\]
This bound is attained by \(m=4\), \(n=8\), since
\[
m^7n^6=2^{14+18}=16^8.
\]

Finally, if \(K=16\), the identity \(m^7n^6=2^{32}\) forces \(m=2^u\), \(n=2^v\) with \(u,v\ge1\). The equation \(7u+6v=32\) makes \(u\) positive and even, and \(7u\le26\), so \(u=2\) and \(v=3\). Thus the minimizing pair is unique, and
\[
m+n=4+8=\boxed{12},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
